title: Unresponsive but possibly aware: voice, hearing, touch, and the humility boundary

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0017 inside-view/nonproof layer; no private testimony, no public rendering, no clinical/spiritual/prognostic authority.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, and seed-cue factoring during rev0017
limitations: Public sources support orientation, vocabulary, and review routing only; they do not authorize claims about any individual dying person’s inner experience.
Inside-view material is high-risk for overclaiming, spiritual proof, clinical misinterpretation, and false reassurance.
Pain, dyspnea, delirium, sedation, dementia, and cardiac-arrest material must route to qualified clinical review before public rendering.
No source in this record should be used to predict time of death, prove awareness, prove afterlife claims, decide treatment, or rank a death as good or bad.

moment.plain_scene: When someone is less responsive or unconscious, witnesses often ask whether speaking, touch, music, or presence still reaches them. The archive can encourage humility and kindness while refusing proof claims.
ordinary_language_queries: should I talk to dying person

content_layers.observation_text: When someone is less responsive or unconscious, witnesses often ask whether speaking, touch, music, or presence still reaches them. The archive can encourage humility and kindness while refusing proof claims.
content_layers.source_synthesis: This quarantined record converts public-source orientation and seed-brief debt into a governed inside-view record. It distinguishes reported experience from inference and blocks proof, prophecy, diagnosis, treatment guidance, and universalization.

interpretation.primary_interpretation: This record says: speak as if presence matters, not because the archive can prove what is heard.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Any future public page must label the evidence channel, preserve uncertainty, and refuse afterlife proof, clinical diagnosis, timing prediction, or required meaning.
interpretation.risk_of_overread: High if one reported experience is treated as universal, if silence is filled with speculation, or if a clinical/spiritual boundary is collapsed.

uncertainties: No private witness account has been collected for this record.
Public sources support evidence-class design and vocabulary, not individual interpretation.
The same utterance or body sign may carry different meanings across people, settings, traditions, and clinical states.
Future contributor review, clinical review, survivor-account review, and cultural review may split, merge, revise, or retire this record.
content_layers.lay_orientation: This record is for recognition and humility: something like this has been reported or witnessed before, but the archive will not pretend to know more than the evidence allows.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future contributors should be asked which evidence channel they are using: what the person said, what was witnessed, what was inferred, what was clinically assessed, what was remembered after recovery, and what remains inaccessible.
language_notes: Do not translate the dying person’s words into a single authorized meaning.
Keep family-search language visible without letting panic-search phrases become diagnosis or proof.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0017 to expand the cube from external witness layers into the evidence-bound inside view of dying, recovery, perception, silence, and non-access.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not publish private dream, vision, utterance, recovery, pain, delirium, dementia, sedation, family, or spiritual details without consent and review.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: present_if visions, ancestors, spirits, prayers, rituals, nonbelief, or tradition-specific meanings appear
safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, prognosis, diagnosis, treatment instruction, verification of death, resuscitation guidance, sedation guidance, therapy protocol, legal/funeral advice, ritual instruction, or proof of consciousness/afterlife.
safety_notes: The dying person’s reported experience is authoritative about their own meaning, not a universal rule.
Do not make silence, unresponsiveness, sedation, or dementia stand for absence of interior life.
Do not make visions, dreams, lucidity, or survivor accounts stand for proof of what death is like for everyone.
When the archive cannot know, it should say it cannot know.

review.review_notes: Rev0017 inside-view records are designed to expose evidence channels and review needs, not to become public copy.
